reasoning_traces.think:
Isotonic calibration constructs a piecewise constant function that maps input probabilities to calibrated outputs while preserving monotonicity. It minimizes sum-of-squared-errors (SSE) subject to ordering constraints. In the example, repeated forecasts at p=0.65 with outcomes 0 and 1 are pooled into a single breakpoint at 0.5. This avoids overfitting and maintains consistency with empirical frequency. The true isotonic fit computes the globally optimal solution using PAVA (Pool Adjacent Violators Algorithm), which iteratively merges adjacent violations until no more exist. A greedy approach would incorrectly assign values like 0.333 and 1.0, violating optimality. The key insight is that grouping forecasts before computing means prevents erroneous splits and ensures valid calibration. This process enables accurate Bayesian updates in GSI and supports reliable decision-making in GSE.
